name: Marco Rubio
role: U.S. Secretary of State (2025-); U.S. Senator from Florida (2011-2025)
summary: A Cuban-American Republican from Florida who rose as a Tea Party senator, co-wrote the 2013 Gang of Eight immigration bill, then moved toward border-first immigration policy. He holds conservative positions on abortion, marriage, guns, drugs and health care, and has hawkish views on China, Cuba, Iran and Venezuela. By 2019 he favored industrial policy and 'common-good capitalism', and as Secretary of State he has defended tariffs, put foreign aid under State Department control and ranked national interest above the post-war global order.

notes: Immigration: co-wrote the 2013 Senate bill with a path to legal status, then said border security must come first; recent position weighted. Trade: supported TPP in 2015-16 and opposed tariffs earlier; by 2019 and as Secretary of State he backs tariffs and industrial policy, and calls free trade a dangerous delusion. Several 2026 items (Venezuela, Iran) are taken from Wikipedia's account of his record. Only positions found in opened sources are recorded; the rest are null. Later pass 2026-11-13 (rules 7): sources tagged by kind. Twenty-five answers rested only on Wikipedia's two articles; eight were re-sourced to his roll-call votes (Voteview: minimum wage, estate tax, balanced budget amendment, Patriot Act, background checks), a Congressional Record speech or his 2025 confirmation hearing, and seventeen are nulled with history because no vote or statement in the sources opened records the position. The later Venezuela and Iran items taken from Wikipedia are no longer used. His 2025 hearing turn says he has fought unilateral executive military action except in imminent self-defence; per the record-over-words rule the interventionism statements (non-intervention) are answered from his Senate votes on war authorisations, with that hearing turn as a listed source. arm-foreign-insurgents is recovered from his 2014 committee questioning. The remaining nulls were searched in the Stanford Congressional Record text, Senate Foreign Relations hearings of 2011-2015 and the Voteview roll calls (Syria AUMF committee vote, First Step Act, creationism, death penalty, two-state: no recorded vote or statement); the full MediaSum set of his turns (about 400 transcripts) was searched by theme for each remaining null; it yielded marijuana, Libya, Apple-encryption, marriage-and-states and green-card-wait quotes used above and nothing on death penalty, creationism, two-state, flat tax, criminal justice or polluter liability without a position; state.gov (his 2026 interviews) now refuses automated access.
